claim: The Citadelle is a 17th-century hexagonal keep (built 1602-1608) housing a maritime history museum across two floors with eleven ground-floor rooms on fishing and trade, plus exhibits on sailors Allard, Suffren and Bouchard, and offers one of the best coastal views.
quote: the dungeon of the Citadel of Saint-Tropez ... offers one of the most beautiful views of the coast ... eleven rooms covering local fishing, coastal trading, shipyards ... General Allard, the Bailli de Suffren, and Hippolyte Bouchard

claim: Citadelle de Saint-Tropez maritime museum admission is EUR 9 per person, with hours 10am-6:30pm April-September and 10am-5:30pm October-March.
quote: The entrance fee is EUR 9 per person ... April 1 to September 30: 10am-6:30pm; October 1 to March 31: 10am-5:30pm

claim: The Citadelle is closed for renovation works with reopening scheduled for 18 April 2026.
quote: La Citadelle is currently closed for works, with reopening scheduled for 18/04/2026

claim: The Musée de l'Annonciade, founded 1922 in a former chapel at Place Georges Grammont, holds works from 1890-1950 (Pointillist, Nabi, Fauve) by Signac, Cross, Matisse, Derain and Marquet, recalling the town's role as an avant-garde painting centre after Signac arrived in 1892.
quote: founded in 1922 ... one of the most active centers of avant-garde painting in the early 20th century ... Signac, Cross, Matisse, Derain, and Marquet

claim: Musée de l'Annonciade entry is EUR 5-6 full / EUR 3.50 reduced, free for under-12s, open Tuesday to Sunday roughly 10am-6pm (later in high summer).
quote: Full price is 5 to 6 €, reduced price is 3.50 € ... free entry for children under 12 ... open from Tuesday to Sunday

claim: La Ponche is the old fishing quarter of Saint-Tropez, a maze of narrow cobbled streets just off the Vieux Port and the town's most picturesque, atmospheric historic area.
quote: La Ponche ... the historic center of Saint-Tropez ... the most picturesque area of the city, with its colorful narrow cobbled streets

claim: The Vieux Port (Old Port) sits at the heart of town, lined with pastel Mediterranean townhouses, cafe terraces and moored yachts; the ochre Notre-Dame de l'Assomption bell tower (1634, restored 1980s) is the town's emblem above an 18th-century church with Italian-style interiors.
quote: ochre-and-sienna bell tower of Notre-Dame de l'Assomption is a defining feature of the Saint-Tropez skyline ... Originally built in 1634 and restored in the 1980s ... the 18th century, is a listed historic site with elegant Italian-style interiors

claim: Place des Lices is a shaded square near the Vieux Port where locals play petanque and which hosts a traditional Provencal market of fruit, vegetables and flowers on Tuesday and Saturday mornings.
quote: Place des Lices is a pleasant shady square ... where the elderly of Saint-Tropez gather to play petanque. On Tuesday and Saturday mornings, a traditional Provencal market takes place

claim: Brigitte Bardot's 1956 film And God Created Woman transformed Saint-Tropez from a sleepy fishing village into a jet-set destination; she bought the La Madrague residence in 1958, drawing stars like Mick Jagger and Eddy Barclay and making the town a jet-set party hub.
quote: And God Created Woman (1956) ... transformed the French Riviera town from a sleepy fishing village into a sizzling jet-set destination ... In 1958, Brigitte Bardot acquired the residence La Madrague ... Mick Jagger ... the international jet-set

claim: Club 55 (club55.fr, iconic chic/classic since 1955), Moorea Plage (party/family, €8 parking), Bagatelle, La Serena (family) and Tahiti Beach are leading Pampelonne clubs with 2026 sunbeds roughly €45-60.
quote: Club 55 | Chic/Classic | €60 | club55.fr ... Moorea Plage | Party/Family | €50-70 | mooreaplage.fr | Established 1952; €8 parking ... Bagatelle | Luxury Party | €60 ... La Serena | Relaxed/Food | €50 ... Tahiti Beach | Family-Friendly | €50

claim: Pampelonne clubs split by vibe: party (Nikki Beach champagne-shower pool parties, Verde Beach, Moorea, Bagatelle, Club 55 celebrity), chic (La Réserve à la Plage, Byblos Beach, Shellona, Club Les Palmiers), and family-friendly (La Serena).
quote: Nikki Beach | Party - Pool-centric with DJ sets, dance performances, champagne showers ... La Reserve a la Plage | Chic - Elegant unwinding ... La Serena | Family - Family-friendly fun ... Club 55 | Party/Celebrity - Legendary since 1955, famous for celebrity-spotting

claim: Pampelonne beach has over 20 different beach clubs including Nikki Beach, Club 55, Bagatelle, Verde Beach, Moorea, La Serena, Tropezina, Tahiti, Bora Bora and Le Lagon.
quote: Pampelonne has over 20 different beach clubs ... Nikki Beach, Club 55, and Bagatelle ... Verde Beach (best food), Moorea (party atmosphere), La Serena (most relaxing) ... Tahiti, Bora Bora Beach, Le Lagon

claim: Plage des Salins is a 500m wild white-sand family beach about 7km north of Saint-Tropez town, with free parking via Moutte park (5-minute walk) and lifeguard cover June-September.
quote: north of the infamous stretch known as Pampelonne beach and about 7km from the town ... white sand beach stretches out over 500 meters ... by the Moutte park with free parking and a five minute shady walk ... family beach and guarded ... not easy to park in the summer but it's free

claim: Plage de la Bouillabaisse sits at the town entrance between Saint-Tropez and Gassin with free public access plus private sections, parking and beach restaurants (Pearl Beach, 270°, La Bouillabaisse), and is rated the best sunset spot.
quote: along the coastline between Saint-Tropez and Gassin ... both private sections and public coastline available to visitors at no cost ... Pearl Beach, 270° by Golfe Azur, and La Bouillabaisse beach club ... best spot to admire the sun going down behind the hills of the Massif des Maures

claim: Pampelonne has six public access points and parking lots (rte de Tahiti, chemin des Moulins, chemin de Tamaris, bd Patch, chemin des Barraques, rte de Bonne Terrasse) with parking from about €5.50; the beach is a 10-minute (~2.8 mile) drive from town with a summer Bus des Plages shuttle.
quote: Public entries and parking for €5.50 are available at one of six access points: rte de Tahiti, chemin des Moulins, chemin de Tamaris, bd Patch, chemin des Barraques and rte de Bonne Terrasse ... around 10 minutes to reach by car from the town centre

claim: Most Pampelonne private clubs rent sunbeds from around €30-40 up to €150 per day depending on club and season, with Club 55 the original and most famous restaurant-club.
quote: most beaches on Pampelonne offer sunbeds from around €30-40, while sunbeds at some venues are priced from €40 up to €150

claim: Pampelonne public paid parking runs roughly €5-10 for a few hours or €15-20 for a full day in peak 2026, with limited free roadside parking and risk of towing for illegal parking.
quote: expect to pay anywhere from 5-10 euros for a few hours, or 15-20 euros for a full day during peak season in 2026 ... Limited free parking is available near Pampelonne Beach, primarily along informal roadside spots ... Illegally parked cars are subject to towing

claim: Plage de la Ponche is Saint-Tropez's most central beach, a tiny 50m free sand-and-pebble cove in the old town reachable only on foot from the port or citadel, with no amenities or beach bars.
quote: the most central beach in Saint-Tropez ... extends for only 50 meters ... only accessible on foot from the port or the citadel ... You won't find any amenities or beach bars here ... free to access

claim: The Saint-Tropez Sentier du Littoral loop is about 12 km (7.48 mi), moderate, ~3h45 walking, with roughly 110 m elevation gain, passing Pointe de la Rabiou, Pointe de Capon and Cap Pinet.
quote: Distance & Duration: 7.48 mi covering approximately 3 hours 45 minutes... gains 361 feet... Pointe de la Rabiou, Pointe de l'Ay, Cap de St-Tropez, Pointe de Capon (former battery), and Cap Pinet... Salins beach

claim: The Sentier du Littoral officially starts at La Ponche, Saint-Tropez's old fishing quarter; a short easy 10-minute walk reaches Plage des Graniers beside the Citadel, and the path is marked with yellow paint and 'Sentier du Littoral' signs.
quote: The 'official' start of the Sentier du Littoral is in La Ponche... Plage des Graniers is a pretty, sandy bay next to the imposing Citadel of St Tropez, easily reached via a 10-minute walk along the Sentier du Littoral coastal path

claim: The Saint-Tropez coastal path runs east from the Tour du Portalet past Baie des Canebiers, Pointe de la Rabiou, Cap des Salins, Pointe de Capon and Cap du Pinet to the white-sand beaches near Tahiti Plage.
quote: begins at the pier in St Tropez under the Tour du Portalet... Baie des Canebiers, Pointe de la Rabiou, Pointe de l'Ay, La Croisette, Cap des Salins, Pointe de Capon, Cap du Pinet... white sandy beaches just past Cap du Pinet

claim: Sea kayaking and paddleboard are available at Tiki Pep's (Escalet/Pampelonne, April-November); La Moune Watersports rents single kayaks at €15/hr, doubles €20/hr and paddleboards €20/hr.
quote: Tiki Pep's... sea kayaking and Stand up paddleboard excursions... Open April to November... La Moune Watersports... Single kayak €15/hour, Double kayak €20/hour, Paddle €20/hour

claim: Saint-Tropez boat and yacht rentals start from around $90/hr, with 30+ boats including powerboats, yachts, pontoons and jet skis, most departing the Vieux Port.
quote: 30+ boat & yacht rentals available starting from $90/hr, with options for powerboats, yachts, pontoons, and jet skis

claim: Les Voiles de Saint-Tropez 2026 runs 26 September-4 October, drawing about 250 boats - classic vessels over a century old, maxi yachts and contemporary racers - organized by the Société Nautique de Saint-Tropez (founded 1862; event first held 1999).
quote: Dates: September 26 - October 4, 2026... about 250 boats comprising three categories: classic vessels (some over a century old), maxi yachts, and contemporary boats... Société Nautique de Saint-Tropez... first organized this event in 1999

claim: Pep's Spirit (Ramatuelle) runs guided electric mountain-bike tours over 300 km of peninsula trails, €60 for 2 hours or €90 for the 3-hour E-Bike & Wine outing with tasting, daily 1 April-30 October, min 4 people.
quote: 300 kms of trails, all levels... €60 for 2-hour tours... €90 for 3-hour tours (includes the E-Bike & Wine experience with tasting)... From 01/04 to 30/10/2026 daily... Minimum group size is 4 people

claim: Gassin sits 8 km from Saint-Tropez and 2.5 km from Ramatuelle, classed among France's Most Beautiful Villages, with the Androuno, the world's narrowest street at 29 cm.
quote: Gassin is located 8 kilometers from Saint-Tropez and 2.5 kilometers from Ramatuelle ... one of the Most Beautiful Villages in France ... the Androuno, the narrowest street in the world at 29 centimeters wide.

claim: Ramatuelle is a hilltop village (village perché) about 10 km southwest of Saint-Tropez with views over the Gulf and narrow streets lined with coloured shutters and bougainvillea.
quote: Ramatuelle is around 10 kilometres to the south west of Saint Tropez ... a striking feature of the Provence landscape, clinging to a hillside ... gorgeous narrow streets lined with coloured shutters and vibrant pink bougainvillea trees.

claim: Grimaud, ~12 km northwest of Saint-Tropez, offers a half-day taking in the 11th/12th-century castle ruins, Saint-Michel church, Saint-Roch mill and the Pont des Fées, then the canal town of Port Grimaud.
quote: In half a day, you can visit the castle, Saint-Michel Church, Saint-Roch Mill, and the Pont des Fées, then head down to the lakeside town of Port Grimaud for a complete change of atmosphere.

claim: Port Grimaud, the 'Little Venice of Provence', was designed in the 1960s by architect François Spoerry so each house has direct water access; explore on foot, by electric boat or water taxi, ~15 min drive from Saint-Tropez.
quote: conceived in the 1960s by visionary architect François Spoerry, who designed the town so that each residence has direct water access ... You can explore on foot, by electric boat or using water taxis

claim: Domaine Tropez in Gassin runs a €20/person guided tour and tasting of 7 estate wines (English Thursdays 11am, French Wednesdays 11am, no reservation), plus chocolate-and-wine pairing from €140 for two; cellar open year-round.
quote: €20 per person; free for under 18 ... visit the winery ... tasting of 7 estate wines ... English: Thursdays at 11:00 AM ... Chocolate & Wine Pairing: €140 for 2 people

claim: The Ramatuelle peninsula holds numerous Côtes de Provence estates with cellar tastings, including Vignobles de Ramatuelle (cooperative, ~70% rosé), Domaine la Tourraque (since 1805), Château des Marres on the Route des Plages, and Le Mas de Pampelonne (year-round cellar tastings).
quote: Le Mas de Pampelonne - 15-hectare domain established in 1886, offering 'sale in the cellar' with tastings available year-round ... Domaine la Tourraque - Operating since 1805

claim: Vignobles de Ramatuelle groups winegrowers from Ramatuelle, Gassin, La Croix Valmer and Saint-Tropez producing AOP Côtes de Provence, with free tasting in the cellar on the road to Escalet beach; Château Volterra in Ramatuelle hosted 1930s/40s celebrities and majors on red wine (65% of output).
quote: taste these wines free of charge in their cellar on the road leading to the splendid Escalet beach ... Château Volterra ... celebrities including Josephine Baker, Marcel Pagnol and Jean Cocteau ... red wines which represent 65% of the production

claim: Boat excursions in the Gulf depart from Sainte-Maxime and Cavalaire-sur-Mer to Porquerolles, Port-Cros and the Îles d'Hyères, plus coastal routes to Les 3 Caps Sauvages and the red Calanques de l'Estérel.
quote: Porquerolles - described as the 'pearl' of the Golden Isles ... Port-Cros - a national park ... Les 3 Caps Sauvages (Cap Taillat, Cap Camarat, Cap Lardier) ... Calanques de l'Estérel - featuring 'crimson rock' cliffs

claim: A full-day Porquerolles cruise from Sainte-Maxime departs ~9:30am and returns ~7:30pm, with adult fares around €48.90 to €51.50.
quote: Departures are at 9:30 am with returns around 7:30 pm, and adult prices range from 48.90 to 51.50 €.

claim: The Place des Lices Provençal market runs Tuesday and Saturday mornings, roughly 8am to 1pm, selling food, clothing, local handicrafts, furniture, plants and flowers.
quote: Market traders offer a range of food products including seasonal fruit and vegetables, fish and seafood, cold cuts and meat, as well as clothing, local handicrafts, furniture, plants and flowers.

claim: Place des Lices is Saint-Tropez's iconic central square, shaded by plane trees and the home of the market and pétanque.
quote: Place des Lices - Saint-Tropez Tourisme

claim: Under the plane trees at Place des Lices, locals and visitors play pétanque - teams of one to three throw boules toward the cochonnet, first to 13 points wins.
quote: Pétanque is played in teams of one to three players, with the goal to throw your boules as close as possible to the small wooden target ball, the cochonnet... The first team to reach 13 points wins.

claim: The tarte tropézienne is a halved brioche filled with pastry cream and buttercream and topped with pearl sugar, created in 1955 by Polish confectioner Alexandre Micka, with the name suggested by Brigitte Bardot during filming of And God Created Woman.
quote: Actress Brigitte Bardot developed a taste for the pastries while she was in Saint-Tropez filming And God Created Woman, and it was in fact she who suggested the name, which Micka registered as a trademark in 1973.

claim: La Tarte Tropézienne, Micka's original house, is the registered brand selling the iconic dessert from its Saint-Tropez boutiques.
quote: La Tarte Tropézienne

claim: Atelier Rondini, founded 1927 at 18-18bis rue Georges Clémenceau, is the oldest Saint-Tropez sandal maker, hand-making the flat leather Tropézienne sandal with four or five straps.
quote: Tropezian Sandals Rondini | The older Sandal Maker of St Tropez

claim: K.Jacques was founded in 1933 by Armenian refugees Jacques and Elise Keklikian at rue Allard, Saint-Tropez, and has handcrafted Tropézienne sandals worn by Picasso, Cocteau, Bardot and Romy Schneider since.
quote: The first chapter starts in 1933... where Jacques and Elise Keklikian opened their modest store/workshop... the charming town started to attract the country's greatest artists: Picasso, Cocteau and even Brigitte Bardot and Romy Schneider, who slipped on their K.Jacques.

claim: Sénéquier, founded 1930 on the Old Port (with the patisserie dating to 1887), is the landmark café known for its bright red terrace chairs overlooking the harbour and its nougat, candied fruit and tarte tropézienne.
quote: Founded in 1930, Senequier café is instantly recognisable thanks to its vibrant red chairs and vintage French decor.

claim: Les Caves du Roy is the legendary nightclub inside the Hotel Byblos at 27 Avenue Foch, open nightly from June 26 to August 29 in 2026 and Fridays/Saturdays in the May/June and September shoulder months.
quote: 27 Avenue Foch, 83990 Saint-Tropez ... June 26-August 29: Open nightly ... September: Fridays and Saturdays

claim: Les Caves du Roy enforces an upscale dress code (no beachwear, no sports/open footwear, no vulgar t-shirts; shirt and dress pants for men, heels appreciated for women), opens roughly 11:30pm to 6am, and entry-level VIP tables start around 1,500 euros, with booking a month ahead advised for summer weekends.
quote: No Beachwear - No Open or Sports Footwear - No Vulgar T-Shirts ... entry level VIP tables start at 1,500 euros ... Book at least one month in advance for summer weekends ... 11:30 PM to 6 AM

claim: Toulon-Hyeres (TLN) is the nearest airport at about 51 km, roughly 50-55 minutes by car/taxi (around 130 euros), with a budget bus option around 3 euros taking close to 2 hours.
quote: Toulon-Hyeres Airport (TLN), located in Toulon and 51 km from the center of Saint-Tropez ... a taxi costs about 130 euros one way and takes about 55 minutes ... The bus goes to Saint Tropez five times a day for around 3 euros one way

claim: Nice-Cote d'Azur (NCE) is the larger, better-connected airport but about 1.5 hours away (1h21 driving best case), with private transfers running 240-275 euros and convoluted public transport via Saint-Raphael taking 3+ hours.
quote: Nice-Cote d'Azur airport is about 1 1/2 hours away depending on traffic ... approximately 1 hour 21 minutes to drive ... A taxi costs between 240 and 275

claim: Les Bateaux Verts run the Sainte-Maxime to Saint-Tropez shuttle in just 15 minutes, with additional crossings from Les Issambres (25 min), Marines de Cogolin (25 min) and Port-Grimaud (20 min), now operating year-round daily roughly 7:30am to 11pm.
quote: regular services to Saint-Tropez from Sainte-Maxime ... Sainte-Maxime (15 min to Saint-Tropez) ... Les Issambres (25 min) ... Marines de Cogolin (25 min) ... Port-Grimaud (20 min)

claim: Les Bateaux Bleus run a separate seasonal sea shuttle from Saint-Raphael's Old Port (Quai Amiral Nomy) to Saint-Tropez taking about 1 hour, daily April-October with hourly summer departures, costing 27 euros one-way / 42 euros round-trip per adult.
quote: departures every hour are provided between 8h30 and 16h30 ... crossing takes about 1 hour ... every day from April to October ... One-way tickets cost 27 euros/adult ... round-trip tickets at 42 euros/adult

claim: Parking du Nouveau Port is the main car park with about 1,400 spaces at 1 Avenue du General de Gaulle, the safest bet for visitors given direct access, with on-street parking charged daily May-October from 8am to 1am.
quote: 1400 spaces plus 24 spaces for people with reduced mobility and 8 bus spaces ... 1 Avenue du General de Gaulle ... On-street parking is charged every day from May to October from 8am to 1am

claim: The shoulder seasons of May, June and September offer the best balance for Saint-Tropez, avoiding July-August peak crowds, traffic, noise and high prices while keeping warm weather, though some top beach clubs and restaurants may not yet be open in early May.
quote: the best times to go are in the shoulder seasons of May, June, and September ... some of the best restaurants and beach clubs might not yet be open in May
